## File: `App.tsx`

# App Component

The `App` component is the main entry point of the React application. It manages the overall state and orchestrates the rendering of various sub-components that make up the user interface.

## Props Interface

The `App` component does not accept any props.

## State & Hooks

The component uses several state variables and hooks to manage its internal state and side effects:

- `allConversations`: An array of conversation objects, initialized using `useState`.
- `activeModels`: An array of currently selected model names, managed with `useState`.
- `selectedCoders`: An array of selected coder IDs, managed with `useState`.
- `projectState`: The current state of the project (idle, running, paused), managed with `useState`.
- `isEditModalOpen`, `isSettingsModalOpen`, `isModelSettingsModalOpen`: Flags to control the visibility of modals, managed with `useState`.
- `projectDirectory`: The current project directory path, managed with `useState`.
- `sessionOutputs`: An object mapping model names to their output strings, managed with `useState`.
- `streamStatuses`: An object mapping model names to their stream statuses, managed with `useState`.
- `streamErrors`: An object mapping model names to their stream error messages, managed with `useState`.
- `projectActionPending`, `promptActionPending`, `discussionActionPending`, `extendActionPending`: Flags indicating whether certain actions are in progress, managed with `useState`.
- `discussionSettings`: The current discussion settings object, managed with `useState`.
- `discussionState`: The current state of the discussion (idle, running, paused), managed with `useState`.
- `discussionStatus`: An object containing detailed information about the discussion status, managed with `useState`.
- `discussionError`: An error message related to the discussion, managed with `useState`.
- `isExtendModalOpen`: A flag indicating whether the extend turns modal is open, managed with `useState`.
- `extendTurnsValue`: The number of turns to extend the discussion by, managed with `useState`.
- `macroConfig`: An object containing macro configurations, managed with `useState`.
- `macrosLoading`: A flag indicating whether macros are being loaded, managed with `useState`.
- `toasts`: An array of toast messages to display, managed with `useState`.
- `waitingOnHuman`, `pendingTurnParticipant`, `humanEnabled`, `bypassHuman`, `humanActionPending`: Variables related to human turn handling, managed with `useState`.

The component also uses several custom hooks and utility functions:

- `useRef`: Used to create references for WebSocket connections and other mutable values.
- `useCallback`: Used to memoize callback functions to prevent unnecessary re-renders.
- `useEffect`: Used to perform side effects based on state changes.

## External Calls

The `App` component interacts with external APIs and services:

- It fetches macro configurations from the `/api/macros` endpoint using `fetch`.
- It sends prompts to the backend using the `/api/control/send-prompt` endpoint.
- It retrieves discussion status using the `/api/discussion/status` endpoint.
- It configures discussions using the `/api/discussion/configure` endpoint.
- It starts and stops discussions using the `/api/discussion/start` and `/api/discussion/stop` endpoints.
- It extends discussions using the `/api/discussion/extend` endpoint.
- It sends human responses using the `/api/discussion/human/submit` endpoint.
- It handles various control actions using the `/api/control/*` endpoints.

The component uses WebSocket connections to establish real-time communication with the backend for streaming model outputs and handling discussion events.

# Component: ControlButton

## Purpose
The `ControlButton` component is a reusable button component designed for use in React applications. It provides a customizable button with an icon, click event handler, and a title attribute for accessibility and tooltips. The component is styled with Tailwind CSS classes to ensure a consistent and visually appealing appearance.

## Props Interface
The `ControlButton` component accepts the following props:

- `icon`: `ReactNode | string` - The icon or text to be displayed inside the button. It can be a ReactNode (e.g., an icon component) or a string representing the icon's name.
- `onClick`: `() => void` - The click event handler function that is triggered when the button is clicked.
- `title`: `string` - The title attribute of the button, which provides additional information or a tooltip when hovering over the button.

## State & Hooks
The `ControlButton` component does not have any internal state or use any React hooks. It is a stateless functional component that relies on the props passed to it for rendering and behavior.

## External Calls
The `ControlButton` component does not make any external API calls or interact with external services. It is a purely presentational component that focuses on rendering the button based on the provided props.

## Usage Example
```jsx
import ControlButton from 'components/ControlButton';

const ExampleComponent = () => {
  const handleClick = () => {
    console.log('Button clicked!');
  };

  return (
    <div>
      <ControlButton
        icon="plus"
        onClick={handleClick}
        title="Add Item"
      />
    </div>
  );
};
```

In this example, the `ControlButton` component is used within the `ExampleComponent`. It displays a button with a "plus" icon, a click event handler that logs a message to the console, and a title attribute set to "Add Item".

# ConversationWindow Component

The `ConversationWindow` component is a React component that displays a conversation window with messages, control buttons, and macro dropdowns. It is used to render a conversation interface with various controls and settings.

## Props Interface

The component accepts the following props:

- `conversation`: An object representing the conversation, with the following properties:
  - `id`: The unique identifier of the conversation.
  - `title`: The title of the conversation.
  - `messages`: An array of message objects, each containing:
    - `role`: The role of the message, either "user" or "assistant".
    - `content`: The content of the message.
- `onControlAction`: A callback function that is called when a control action is triggered. It takes two parameters:
  - `modelName`: The name of the model associated with the conversation.
  - `action`: The action to be performed.
- `onMacroTrigger`: A callback function that is called when a macro is triggered. It takes two parameters:
  - `agentName`: The name of the agent associated with the macro.
  - `macroName`: The name of the macro that was triggered.
- `status`: The current status of the conversation, which can be one of the following:
  - "ready": The conversation is ready.
  - "processing": The conversation is being processed.
  - "error": An error occurred during the conversation.
- `projectState`: The current state of the project, which can be one of the following:
  - "idle": The project is idle.
  - "running": The project is running.
  - "paused": The project is paused.
- `onEditInstructions`: A callback function that is called when the instructions for a conversation are edited. It takes one parameter:
  - `modelName`: The name of the model associated with the conversation.
- `onConfigureSettings`: A callback function that is called when the settings for a conversation are configured. It takes one parameter:
  - `modelName`: The name of the model associated with the conversation.
- `output`: The output of the conversation.
- `streamStatus`: The current status of the stream, which can be one of the following:
  - "idle": The stream is idle.
  - "connecting": The stream is connecting.
  - "streaming": The stream is streaming.
  - "error": An error occurred during the stream.
- `errorMessage`: An optional error message to be displayed.
- `macros`: An optional object containing macro definitions, where the keys are the macro names and the values are the corresponding `MacroDefinition` objects.

## State & Hooks

The component uses the following state and hooks:

- `scrollContainerRef`: A ref to the scroll container element.
- `isStickyRef`: A ref to track whether the scroll is sticky or not.
- `ignoreScrollRef`: A ref to ignore scroll events temporarily.
- `STICKY_THRESHOLD_PX`: A constant representing the threshold in pixels for sticky scrolling.

The component uses the following hooks:

- `useLayoutEffect`: Used to perform side effects after the component is rendered and the layout is updated. It is used to handle scrolling behavior.
- `useRef`: Used to create mutable refs for accessing DOM elements and storing state.
- `useMemo`: Used to memoize the `macroGroups` and `availableCategories` objects to avoid unnecessary re-computation.

## External Calls

The component does not make any external API calls or interact with external services directly. It relies on the provided props and callbacks to handle user interactions and update the conversation state.

# EditInstructionsModal

## Purpose
The `EditInstructionsModal` component is a React modal that allows users to edit and save instructions for a specific model. It fetches the initial instructions from an API when the modal opens and sends the updated instructions back to the API when the user saves the changes.

## Props Interface
The component accepts the following props:
- `modelName` (string): The name of the model for which the instructions are being edited.
- `isOpen` (boolean): A flag indicating whether the modal is open or closed.
- `onClose` (function): A callback function to close the modal.
- `projectDirectory` (string): The directory of the project.
- `apiBaseUrl` (string): The base URL of the API.

## State & Hooks
The component uses the following state variables and hooks:
- `content` (string): The current content of the instructions, which is updated whenever the user types in the textarea.
- `isLoading` (boolean): A flag indicating whether the instructions are being loaded from the API.
- `useEffect`: A hook that fetches the initial instructions from the API when the modal opens and the `modelName` prop changes.
- `useState`: A hook that manages the `content` and `isLoading` state variables.

## External Calls
The component makes the following external API calls:
- When the modal opens and the `modelName` prop changes, it fetches the initial instructions from the API using the `fetch` function. The API endpoint is constructed using the `apiBaseUrl`, `modelName`, and `projectDirectory` props. The fetched instructions are then stored in the `content` state variable.
- When the user clicks the "Save" button, it sends the updated instructions to the API using the `fetch` function. The API endpoint is constructed using the `apiBaseUrl` and `modelName` props. The `content` and `projectDirectory` props are sent as the request body in JSON format. If the request is successful, the modal is closed by calling the `onClose` callback.

## Exported Functions
The component does not export any functions. It is a self-contained component that can be imported and used in other parts of the application.

# Component Name & Purpose

**Component Name:** `MacroDropdown`

**Purpose:** The `MacroDropdown` component is a React component designed to display a dropdown menu containing a list of macros. It allows users to select a macro from the list, which triggers a callback function to handle the selected macro. The component is designed to be flexible and customizable, accepting various props to control its behavior and appearance.

# Props Interface (inputs)

The `MacroDropdown` component accepts the following props:

- `agent` (type: `string`): The name of the agent associated with the macros.
- `category` (type: `MacroCategory`): The category of the macros.
- `macros` (type: `MacroEntry[]`): An array of macro entries, where each entry contains a `name` and a `macro` object.
- `disabled` (type: `boolean`, optional): A flag indicating whether the dropdown should be disabled. Default is `false`.
- `onSelect` (type: `(macroName: string) => void`): A callback function that is called when a macro is selected. It receives the name of the selected macro as an argument.

# State & Hooks

The `MacroDropdown` component uses the following state and hooks:

- `open` (type: `boolean`): A state variable that tracks whether the dropdown menu is open or closed. It is managed using the `useState` hook.
- `menuRef` (type: `React.RefObject<HTMLDivElement>`): A ref used to store a reference to the dropdown menu element. It is used to detect clicks outside the dropdown menu and close it accordingly. It is managed using the `useRef` hook.
- `sortedMacros` (type: `MacroEntry[]`): A memoized array of sorted macro entries. It is derived from the `macros` prop using the `useMemo` hook. The macros are sorted based on their labels (either the macro description or the macro name).

# External Calls

The `MacroDropdown` component does not make any external API calls or interact with external services. It solely relies on the props passed to it and manages its own state internally.

The component renders a dropdown menu with the following structure:

- A button that displays the icon representing the macro category and a chevron icon. Clicking this button toggles the opening and closing of the dropdown menu.
- If the dropdown is open, it displays a list of macro entries. Each entry is rendered as a clickable button that displays the macro label and an optional secondary label (e.g., shortcut or command). Clicking a macro entry triggers the `onSelect` callback with the selected macro name and closes the dropdown.

The dropdown menu is styled using CSS classes and is positioned absolutely relative to its parent element. It has a maximum height and allows vertical scrolling if the content exceeds the height limit.

Overall, the `MacroDropdown` component provides a reusable and customizable dropdown menu for selecting macros based on the provided props and state management.

# Component Name & Purpose

**Component Name:** `ModelSettingsModal`

**Purpose:** The `ModelSettingsModal` component is a modal dialog that allows users to view and edit model settings for a specific project. It fetches the model settings from an API, displays them in a user-friendly format, and allows users to save changes or reset the settings to their defaults.

## Props Interface (inputs)

The component accepts the following props:

- `isOpen`: A boolean indicating whether the modal is open or closed.
- `onClose`: A callback function to close the modal.
- `modelName`: The name of the model for which the settings are being edited.
- `projectDirectory`: The directory of the project for which the settings are being edited.
- `apiBaseUrl`: The base URL of the API to fetch the model settings.

## State & Hooks

The component uses the following state variables and hooks:

- `fields`: An array of `EditableField` objects representing the model settings fields.
- `loading`: A boolean indicating whether the component is currently loading the model settings.
- `saving`: A boolean indicating whether the component is currently saving the changes.
- `error`: A string containing an error message, if any.
- `successMessage`: A string containing a success message, if any.
- `notes`: A string containing any additional notes related to the model settings.
- `useEffect`: A hook to fetch the model settings when the modal is opened.
- `useMemo`: A hook to compute the `modalTitle` based on the `modelName`.
- `useCallback`: A hook to memoize the `mapFields` function.

## External Calls

The component makes the following external calls:

- `fetchSettings`: An asynchronous function that fetches the model settings from the API using the `fetch` function. It is called when the modal is opened or when the `fetchSettings` function is invoked.
- `buildOverrides`: A function that builds an object containing the overrides for the model settings based on the user input.
- `handleSave`: An asynchronous function that saves the overrides to the API using the `fetch` function. It is called when the user clicks the "Save Overrides" button.
- `handleReset`: An asynchronous function that resets the model settings to their defaults by making a DELETE request to the API using the `fetch` function. It is called when the user clicks the "Reset to Defaults" button.

## Exported Functions

The component does not export any functions.

# Component: ProjectSettingsModal

## Purpose
The `ProjectSettingsModal` component is a modal dialog that allows users to select a project directory, create new folders within it, and configure discussion settings for a project. It provides a user interface for browsing the file system, creating folders, and saving project settings.

## Props Interface
The component accepts the following props:
- `isOpen` (boolean): Indicates whether the modal is open or closed.
- `onClose` (function): A callback function to close the modal.
- `projectDirectory` (string): The initial project directory path.
- `discussionSettings` (DiscussionSettings): The initial discussion settings.
- `availableModels` (string[]): An array of available models for the starting model.
- `onSave` (function): A callback function to save the project settings.
- `apiBaseUrl` (string): The base URL for API requests.

## State & Hooks
The component uses the following state variables and hooks:
- `currentPath` (string): The current path in the file system.
- `contents` (FileSystemItem[]): An array of file system items (files and directories) in the current path.
- `newFolderName` (string): The name of the new folder being created.
- `localSettings` (DiscussionSettings): The local copy of discussion settings that can be modified by the user.
- `saving` (boolean): Indicates whether the settings are being saved.
- `saveError` (string | null): An error message if saving the settings fails.

The component uses the following hooks:
- `useState`: To manage the state variables mentioned above.
- `useEffect`: To perform side effects when the component mounts or when certain dependencies change.
- `useCallback`: To memoize the `browsePath` function and avoid unnecessary re-renders.

## External Calls
The component makes the following external API calls:
- `fetch`: It makes HTTP requests to the API server to browse the file system, create folders, and prepare the project directory. The API endpoints used are:
  - `GET /api/fs/browse`: Retrieves the contents of a directory.
  - `POST /api/fs/create-folder`: Creates a new folder in the specified path.
  - `POST /api/fs/prepare-project`: Prepares the project directory for saving settings.

The component uses the `apiBaseUrl` prop to construct the API URLs by removing any trailing slashes and appending the appropriate endpoint paths.

## Summary
The `ProjectSettingsModal` component provides a user interface for selecting a project directory, creating new folders, and configuring discussion settings. It handles user interactions, manages state, and makes API calls to interact with the backend. The component is designed to be reusable and can be easily integrated into other parts of the application.

# PromptInput Component

## Purpose
The `PromptInput` component is a React component designed for a chat interface where users can input prompts, select multiple coders (models), and send the prompt to the selected models. It also includes functionality for human turn interactions, bypass toggles, and skipping turns.

## Props Interface

### Input Props
- `coders`: An array of `Coder` objects, each containing an `id` and a `title`.
- `selectedCoders`: An array of selected coder IDs.
- `onSelectedCodersChange`: A callback function to update the selected coders.
- `onSendPrompt`: A callback function to send the prompt to the selected coders.
- `disabled`: A boolean to disable the component (default: `false`).
- `sending`: A boolean indicating if the prompt is being sent (default: `false`).
- `waitingOnHuman`: A boolean indicating if it's the human's turn (default: `false`).
- `pendingTurnParticipant`: A string or `null` indicating the pending turn participant.
- `humanEnabled`: A boolean indicating if human interaction is enabled (default: `false`).
- `bypassHuman`: A boolean to bypass human interaction (default: `false`).
- `onHumanSubmit`: A callback function to handle human submission.
- `onHumanSkip`: A callback function to skip the human turn.
- `onToggleBypass`: A callback function to toggle the bypass state.
- `humanActionPending`: A boolean indicating if a human action is pending (default: `false`).

## State & Hooks
- `prompt`: A state variable to hold the current prompt text, managed by `useState`.

## External Calls
- `handleSend`: Sends the prompt to the selected coders or all coders if none are selected.
- `handleHumanSubmit`: Submits the human response.
- `handleHumanSkip`: Skips the human turn.
- `handleToggleBypass`: Toggles the bypass state.

## Summary
The `PromptInput` component is a versatile input area for a chat interface, allowing users to input prompts, select multiple models, and interact with human turns. It includes state management for the prompt text and selected models, and integrates with various callback functions to handle sending prompts, human interactions, and bypass toggles.

## File: `components\SessionModelSelector.tsx`

# SessionModelSelector Component

## Purpose
The `SessionModelSelector` component is a React component that allows users to select active models from a list of available models. It displays a list of checkboxes for each model, and users can toggle the selection of each model. The selected models are managed through the `activeModels` prop, and any changes to the selection are communicated to the parent component via the `onActiveModelsChange` callback.

## Props Interface
The component accepts the following props:
- `allModels`: An array of strings representing all available models.
- `activeModels`: An array of strings representing the currently selected active models.
- `onActiveModelsChange`: A callback function that is called when the selection of active models changes. It takes an array of strings as its argument.

## State & Hooks
The component does not have any local state or use any hooks. It relies on the `activeModels` prop to determine the current selection of active models and updates the selection by calling the `onActiveModelsChange` callback whenever a model is toggled.

## External Calls
The component does not make any external calls or interact with APIs. It is a self-contained component that manages the selection of active models locally.

## Component Code
```tsx
import React from 'react';

interface SessionModelSelectorProps {
  allModels: string[];
  activeModels: string[];
  onActiveModelsChange: (activeModels: string[]) => void;
}

const SessionModelSelector: React.FC<SessionModelSelectorProps> = ({
  allModels,
  activeModels,
  onActiveModelsChange,
}) => {
  const toggleModel = (model: string) => {
    const newActiveModels = activeModels.includes(model)
      ? activeModels.filter((m) => m !== model)
      : [...activeModels, model];
    onActiveModelsChange(newActiveModels);
  };

  return (
    <div className="flex justify-center items-center gap-4 py-4">
      <span className="text-gray-400 font-semibold">Active Models:</span>
      {allModels.map((model) => (
        <label key={model} className="flex items-center gap-2 cursor-pointer">
          <input
            type="checkbox"
            checked={activeModels.includes(model)}
            onChange={() => toggleModel(model)}
            className="w-4 h-4 rounded border-[#3e4451] bg-[#1e1e1e] text-blue-600 focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:ring-offset-0 cursor-pointer"
          />
          <span className="text-gray-200">{model}</span>
        </label>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
};

export default SessionModelSelector;
```

# Component: `main.tsx`

## Purpose
The `main.tsx` file serves as the entry point for the React application. It sets up the root component and renders the `App` component within a `StrictMode` wrapper. The `StrictMode` component helps identify potential issues and ensures that the application adheres to best practices.

## Component Hierarchy
- `main.tsx`
  - `StrictMode`
    - `App`

## External Dependencies
- `react`: The core React library.
- `react-dom`: Provides DOM-specific methods for React.
- `react-dom/client`: Provides client-side rendering methods for React.
- `./index.css`: The main CSS file for the application.
- `./App.tsx`: The root component of the application.

## Code Explanation
```tsx
import { StrictMode } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import App from './App.tsx';
import './index.css';

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <App />
  </StrictMode>
);
```

1. The `StrictMode` component is imported from the `react` library. It is used to enable strict mode in the application.

2. The `createRoot` function is imported from `react-dom/client`. It is used to create a root instance for rendering the React application.

3. The `App` component is imported from the `./App.tsx` file. It represents the root component of the application.

4. The `index.css` file is imported to apply global styles to the application.

5. The `createRoot` function is called with `document.getElementById('root')!` as the argument. It creates a root instance for rendering the React application. The `!` is used to assert that the element with the ID 'root' exists in the DOM.

6. The `render` method is called on the root instance, passing a JSX element that wraps the `App` component inside the `StrictMode` component.

7. The `App` component is rendered within the `StrictMode` component, which ensures that the application adheres to strict mode guidelines.

## Summary
The `main.tsx` file sets up the React application by rendering the `App` component within a `StrictMode` wrapper. It serves as the entry point for the application and ensures that the application follows best practices and identifies potential issues.

# DiscussionSettings Component

## Purpose
The `DiscussionSettings` component is responsible for managing and displaying the settings related to a discussion feature in a React application. It allows users to configure various aspects of the discussion, such as the maximum number of turns, the starting model, discussion topic, and other settings.

## Props Interface
The component accepts the following props:

```typescript
interface DiscussionSettingsProps {
  maxTurns: number;
  startingModel: string;
  discussionTopic: string;
  includeHistory: boolean;
  logLevel: string;
}
```

## State & Hooks
The component maintains the following state and uses the following hooks:

```typescript
const [maxTurns, setMaxTurns] = useState<number>(props.maxTurns);
const [startingModel, setStartingModel] = useState<string>(props.startingModel);
const [discussionTopic, setDiscussionTopic] = useState<string>(props.discussionTopic);
const [includeHistory, setIncludeHistory] = useState<boolean>(props.includeHistory);
const [logLevel, setLogLevel] = useState<string>(props.logLevel);
```

## External Calls
The component does not make any external API calls. It solely manages the state and rendering of the discussion settings based on the provided props.

## Usage
The `DiscussionSettings` component can be used as follows:

```jsx
<DiscussionSettings
  maxTurns={10}
  startingModel="model1"
  discussionTopic="Topic 1"
  includeHistory={true}
  logLevel="info"
/>
```

The component will render the appropriate input fields and controls based on the provided props, allowing users to modify the discussion settings. The updated values will be stored in the component's state and can be accessed or used as needed.

## File: `vite-env.d.ts`

# vite-env.d.ts

## Purpose
The `vite-env.d.ts` file is a TypeScript declaration file used in Vite projects to provide type definitions for environment variables and other global types.

## Content
The file contains a single line of code:
```typescript
/// <reference types="vite/client" />
```

### Explanation
- The `/// <reference types="vite/client" />` directive is a TypeScript triple-slash directive that instructs the TypeScript compiler to include the type definitions from the `@types/vite/client` package.
- This package provides type definitions for Vite's built-in client-side APIs and global variables, such as `import.meta.env` and `import.meta.glob`.

## Usage
This file is typically placed in the root directory of a Vite project and is automatically picked up by the TypeScript compiler. It allows you to use Vite-specific types and APIs in your TypeScript code without any additional configuration.

By including this file, you can access Vite's client-side APIs and global variables with proper type checking and autocompletion support in your TypeScript code.

## Summary
The `vite-env.d.ts` file is a TypeScript declaration file used in Vite projects to provide type definitions for Vite's built-in client-side APIs and global variables. It enables type checking and autocompletion support for Vite-specific types and APIs in your TypeScript code.
